articles.title: Goose Is Not a Flisk Language. Here Is What to Run Instead
articles.excerpt: flisk resource api --type backend --language goose will not scaffold a Goose service. I checked the provider guide and the CLI readme. The registered backend languages are Python, Go, Rust, and Node.…
articles.body: flisk resource api --type backend --language goose will not scaffold a Goose service. I checked the provider guide and the CLI readme. The registered backend languages are Python, Go, Rust, and Node. Omit --language and you still get Bun + Hono, byte for byte with the old scaffold. If you meant the Goose programming language (memory-safe, no heap allocator, no GC), Flisk's own rule is explicit: a language without a provider uses --type bring-your-own and your Dockerfile. This post is that path, on a local stack only. Flisk does not deploy this.
articles.author: flisk

articles.title: Our Benchmark No Longer Takes the Agent's Word for It
articles.excerpt: Sorry this week's post is a little late. We have been heads-down shipping a new evidence feature for Favur Evals, and this post is about it. Ask a coding agent if it is done and it says yes. Since Oct…
articles.body: Sorry this week's post is a little late. We have been heads-down shipping a new evidence feature for Favur Evals, and this post is about it. Ask a coding agent if it is done and it says yes. Since October 19, Favur Evals no longer takes its word for it. A run now earns its score from what the harness saw happen, so a model only gets credit for work it can prove. The agent's answer is still worth reading. It will list the tests it ran, the files it changed and the criteria it met, and most of the time that list is honest. The trouble is that the list is the agent's own account of its work, written by the same model that did the work, and nothing in it tells you which lines were seen to happen and which were only said.

articles.body: 1. Introduction: A Growing Market, an Underserved Meeting Italy's AI market hit €1.8 billion in 2025 , up 50% year over year, according to the Politecnico di Milano's AI Observatory. 46% of that market came from generative AI or hybrid projects. 71% of large Italian companies had launched at least one AI project, against just 8% of SMEs. And by August 2026, AI assistants reached 18.9 million unique visitors in Italy , double the roughly 9 million of January 2025 (Sensemakers on Comscore data). Only 23% of Italian workers see their meetings as genuinely useful, and 56% still don't use AI to manage them (ASUS Business survey). You can have a €1.8 billion market and still have a meeting culture that runs on manual notes and post-call memory. The gap isn't transcription.

articles.title: I Built an App That Answers From Your Own Documents, With the Source
articles.excerpt: I built Xyterna, and this is a 98-second look at it with the real app. The idea is simple: you add receipts, bills, warranties and documents as they come in, as photos, files or whole folders. Xyterna…
articles.body: I built Xyterna, and this is a 98-second look at it with the real app. The idea is simple: you add receipts, bills, warranties and documents as they come in, as photos, files or whole folders. Xyterna reads them, keeps the original file, and organizes what matters into records that stay connected. Two design decisions mattered most to me: Every answer points back to its source. Ask "When does my warranty run out?" and you get the answer plus a link to the exact document it came from, so you can check it. It doesn't guess. When dates are unclear or two documents disagree, it says so and asks you, rather than quietly picking one. On top of that, Home surfaces bills, renewals and dates found in your documents, and reports group records by topic for export as a spreadsheet or PDF.

articles.title: Why AI Coding Feels Faster (While Your Sprints Slow Down)
articles.excerpt: If you work on a mature codebase, you have probably felt the weird disconnect around AI coding tools over the past year. In the moment, sitting in your IDE, you feel noticeably faster. You ask an agen…
articles.body: If you work on a mature codebase, you have probably felt the weird disconnect around AI coding tools over the past year. In the moment, sitting in your IDE, you feel noticeably faster. You ask an agent for a new endpoint or a state machine refactor, and 200 lines of clean-looking TypeScript or Java appear in ten seconds. Then you look at your team's sprint board on Friday. Cycle times haven't moved. Pull request review queues are backed up worse than before, and subtle regression bugs keep slipping into staging. In a landmark randomized controlled trial conducted by METR (Model Evaluation & Threat Research), researchers put a stopwatch on experienced open-source developers working across mature codebases.
articles.author: binith

articles.title: Patching PHP 5.6 to 8.1 for PHP2Shell on old Ubuntu servers by rebuilding RunCloud's PHP
articles.excerpt: On October 21, 2026, PHP shipped fixes for PHP2Shell, but only for PHP 8.2 and newer. Our hosting panel, RunCloud, only patches those versions too. Most of our older WordPress sites run on PHP 5.6 to…
articles.body: On October 21, 2026, PHP shipped fixes for PHP2Shell, but only for PHP 8.2 and newer. Our hosting panel, RunCloud, only patches those versions too. Most of our older WordPress sites run on PHP 5.6 to 8.1, on Ubuntu releases as old as 16.04. So that evening we rebuilt PHP ourselves: every old version, for every Ubuntu release on our servers, with RunCloud's own build flags, and swapped in only the patched binaries. This article shows how, what broke on the way, and how we checked that nothing changed for the sites. Everything below was done on October 21, 2026: builds and tests on our own workstation, deploys and checks on our servers. Where a fact comes from someone else, I link the source. Server and client names are left out.

articles.title: Evaluating DoD's DIB CS Program: Insights on Cybersecurity Implementation and Effectiveness for Suppliers
articles.excerpt: Introduction The Defense Industrial Base Cybersecurity (DIB CS) Program, formally designated as DCISE3, is a voluntary initiative spearheaded by the Department of Defense Cyber Crime Center (DC3) to f…
articles.body: Introduction The Defense Industrial Base Cybersecurity (DIB CS) Program , formally designated as DCISE3 , is a voluntary initiative spearheaded by the Department of Defense Cyber Crime Center (DC3) to fortify cybersecurity defenses among suppliers within the Department of Defense (DoD) supply chain. Designed to counter the escalating sophistication and frequency of cyber threats targeting critical defense infrastructure, the program integrates advanced monitoring, threat intelligence sharing, and incident response capabilities. Its strategic importance is underscored by the growing exploitation of supply chain vulnerabilities by cyber adversaries, which directly imperils the operational integrity of DoD systems and broader national security.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. articles.title: Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' depicts the sky on July 22, 1889, researchers find
articles.excerpt: Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night."
articles.body: Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it.
